subject: pigeon
title: City Birds Let Men Get Three Feet Closer Than Women

scenes.text: City birds treat women differently from men. Nobody knows why.
Scientists walked up to birds in seven European cities. Over two thousand seven hundred times.
Pigeons, sparrows, blackbirds, magpies. Thirty-seven species.
Each pair of walkers was a man and a woman of the same height, in similar clothes.
Yet birds fled about one metre sooner from the woman. Every country, almost every species.
Walk, body shape, scent? Untested. So next time a pigeon flies off, ask who's walking.

description:
A study in People and Nature tested 37 urban bird species in five European countries. Birds let men approach about one metre, roughly three feet, closer than women before flying away.
The men and women were expert ornithologists matched for height and clothing. Gait, body shape and scent are possible explanations, but none has been tested.
Have you noticed birds acting differently around different people?
first_comment: The researchers' best guess is the way people walk, which they did not control for. Have birds ever let you get unusually close?
